text: This guide explains how taxes work in Germany, and how to pay less taxes.

section: The taxes you pay in Germany
text: All German residents must pay taxes. These are the taxes to pay: Income and wage tax(Einkommensteuer,Lohnsteuer) Health insurance(Krankenversicherung) Long-term care insurance(Pflegeversicherung) Public pension insurance(gesetzliche Rentenversicherung) Unemployment insurance(Arbeitslosenversicherung) Church tax(Kirchensteuer) Solidarity surcharge(Solidaritätszuschlag) If you are an employee, your employer collects taxes directly from your paycheck. If you are self-employed, you pay taxes bybank transferordirect debit. Income from investments is taxed differently.4You pay: Capital gains tax (Kapitalertragsteuer) Church tax(Kirchensteuer) Solidarity surcharge(Solidaritätszuschlag)

section: The taxes you pay in Germany
title: Income and wage tax
text: All German residents pay income tax (Einkommensteuer). This tax is a percentage of your income. It’s a progressive tax, so if you earn more, you pay a bigger percentage of your income.3 If you earn less than €12,348per year, you pay no income tax. If you earn themedian income, your income tax is around 18% of your income. The maximum income tax is 45% of your income.1 If you are an employee, you pay a wage tax (Lohnsteuer) on every paycheck. This is a prepayment of yourestimatedincome tax. If you pay too much wage tax, you can make atax declarationand get money back. Usually, tips are not taxed.6

section: The taxes you pay in Germany
title: Health insurance
text: All German residents must have health insurance (Krankenversicherung). Health insurance pays for your healthcare when you are sick. There are three types of health insurance: Public health insurance. It costs a percentage of your income. Private health insurance. The cost is set by the health insurer. Expat health insurance. The cost is set by the health insurer. If you are an employee, your employer pays half of it. If you earn less than €565per month, you can use your parents’ or spouse’s health insurance for free. Students get a cheaper tariff. Calculate the cost of German health insurance and see health insurance options for employees, students and freelancers. This tool requires JavaScript to work. section: The taxes you pay in Germany
title: Long-term care insurance
text: Long-term care insurance (Pflegeversicherung) pays for your healthcare when you are old. It costs 2.6% to 4.2% of your income. If you have a job, your employer pays 1.8% and you pay the rest. Use myhealth insurance calculatorto calculate yourPflegeversicherung.

section: The taxes you pay in Germany
title: Public pension insurance
text: All employees must pay into thepublic pension system. It costs 18.6% of your income. If you are an employee, your employer pays half of it, so you pay 9.3%. If you are self-employed, public pension insurance is usually optional. If you don’t pay public pension insurance, you must make your own retirement plans.

section: The taxes you pay in Germany
title: Unemployment insurance
text: Unemployment insurance (Arbeitslosenversicherung) pays a percentage of your salary if youlose your job. It costs 1.3% of your income. The maximum cost is €109.85per month.7

section: The taxes you pay in Germany
title: Church tax
text: If you are a member of certain churches, you pay a church tax. It’s a percentage of your income tax. You also pay church tax on investment income.8 If you live in Baden-Württemberg or Bavaria, it’s 8% of yourincome tax. In other states it’s 9% of your income tax. You stop paying church tax by leaving the church.

section: The taxes you pay in Germany
title: Solidarity surcharge
text: If you pay more than €20,350per year inincome tax, you must pay a solidarity surcharge (Solidaritätszuschlag). It’s a percentage of your income tax. You also pay a solidarity surcharge on investment income.8 German tax calculator

section: The taxes you pay in Germany
title: Capital gains tax
text: The capital gains tax (Kapitalertragsteuer) is a 25% tax on profits from investments. It applies to profit, interests and dividends from stocks, ETFs and other investments. It does not apply to cryptocurrencies.5The first €1,000per year are tax-free.9 Most German brokers deduct this tax automatically when you sell stocks or receive dividends. You must also paychurch taxand asolidarity surchargeon investments.8

All German households must pay theTV tax. If you run a business, you might need to pay thetrade tax. Most things you buy have thevalue added taxincluded in the price. There is also thevehicle tax, thedog tax,property taxand a few others.

If you don’t pay for it, and you don’t getunemployment benefits. Public pension insurance. If you don’t pay for it, and you don’t get a public pension. You must make your own retirement plans. Your business must also pay… Trade tax–More information Value Added Tax(VAT) –More information IHKmembership fee (if you have aGewerbe) –Fee calculator Cost of running a business Since you are self-employed, your employer does not pay half of your health insurance, pension insurance or unemployment insurance. This means that you pay twice as much for social contributions.

Your tax class affects how yourwage taxis calculated. It does not affect how muchincome taxyou pay. It only changes how much income tax you payin advance, as wage tax. You can change your tax class online withELSTER. If you are self-employed, you might not have a tax class, because you don’t need to calculate your wage tax.2 There are 6 tax classes: Tax class 1If you are not married, and you are not in any other tax class. Tax class 2If you are not married, and you raise children alone. You get more tax benefits. Tax class 3If you are married, and you earn more than your spouse. If you are in tax class 3, your spouse is in tax class 5. Tax class 4If you are married, and you and your spouse have similar incomes. If you are in tax class 4, your spouse is also in tax class 4. Tax class 5If you are married, and you earn less than your spouse. If you are in tax class 5, your spouse is in tax class 3. Tax class 6This is the tax class for a second job. If you don’t have a tax ID, your employer might put you in tax class 6. You have no tax benefits, and you pay more wage tax.
